Privacy Policy

Information pursuant to Articles 13 and 14 of the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR)

1. Controller

Sebastijan-Aleksandar Kerčulj, sole proprietor (PutzELF)

Simmeringer Hauptstraße 24, 1110 Vienna, Austria

Phone: +43 676 630 01 67

Email: office@putzelf.com

2. General principles

We process personal data only insofar as this is necessary for the purposes described below. The legal bases are in particular the performance of pre-contractual measures and contracts, legal obligations, legitimate interests and—in the case of optional services—your consent. Data is deleted or anonymized as soon as the purpose no longer applies and no statutory retention or evidentiary obligations remain.

3. Hosting and server log files

The website is hosted by Hetzner Online GmbH, Industriestraße 25, 91710 Gunzenhausen, Germany. When the website is accessed, the server processes, in particular, the IP address, date and time, page or file accessed, amount of data transferred, browser type, operating system and referrer URL. The processing serves the secure, stable and error-free operation of the website and is based on Article 6(1)(f) GDPR. Our legitimate interest lies in the secure operation of our online offering. Server log files are generally deleted no later than 14 days, unless a security-relevant incident makes longer retention necessary. An agreement on processing on our behalf pursuant to Article 28 GDPR is in place with the hosting provider.

4. Appointment inquiries and offer preparation

If you submit a non-binding appointment inquiry through the website, we process the contact details you entered, the address of the property to be cleaned, information about the requested service, the requested appointment and the estimated duration, as well as voluntary comments. In addition, the IP address and time of receipt may be logged to detect technical errors and misuse.

The processing serves to handle your inquiry, check availability, prepare an offer and—after conclusion of a contract—perform and invoice the order. The legal basis is Article 6(1)(b) GDPR; for technical security, Article 6(1)(f) GDPR.

Inquiries that do not lead to a contract are generally deleted after six months, unless longer storage is necessary to handle an open matter or to defend or pursue claims. Contract and invoice documents are retained in accordance with statutory retention obligations, generally for seven years.

5. Contact

When you contact us by telephone, email or contact form, we process the contact details you provided and the content of your message to handle your request and for any necessary follow-up questions. The legal basis is Article 6(1)(b) GDPR if the inquiry is directed at a contract or pre-contractual measures; otherwise, Article 6(1)(f) GDPR. Our legitimate interest lies in handling business and other inquiries. The data is deleted when the matter has been dealt with and no statutory retention or evidentiary interests stand in the way.

6. Service teams and subcontractors

To plan and perform an order, the employees or contractually engaged subcontractors assigned to it receive only the information required for this purpose, in particular name, property address, appointment, access information and service-related instructions. The legal basis is Article 6(1)(b) GDPR. Assigned personnel are required to maintain confidentiality. Where a service provider processes personal data exclusively on our behalf, an agreement pursuant to Article 28 GDPR is concluded.

7. Job applications

If you apply for a job, we process the contact, CV, qualification and application data you provided to carry out the application procedure on the basis of Article 6(1)(b) GDPR and the relevant employment-law provisions. After the procedure has ended, we store the documents for up to seven months on the basis of Article 6(1)(f) GDPR. Our legitimate interest lies in documenting the selection procedure and establishing or defending possible claims. Longer retention on file takes place only with your separate consent.

8. Inquiries from prospective business partners

For an inquiry through “Become a partner” or another channel, we process, in particular, company name, contact person, contact details, location and message to assess and initiate a collaboration. The legal basis is Article 6(1)(b) GDPR insofar as pre-contractual measures are concerned; otherwise, Article 6(1)(f) GDPR. Inquiries that are not pursued are generally deleted after six months, unless statutory retention or evidentiary interests stand in the way.

9. Cookies and consent management

Strictly necessary cookies or comparable storage technologies may be used for the technical operation of the website. This includes, in particular, storing your language, location selection and consent decision. The legal basis is Section 165(3) TKG 2021; insofar as personal data is processed, Article 6(1)(f) GDPR.

Optional analytics, marketing and map services are activated only after you have consented through the consent banner. The legal bases are Article 6(1)(a) GDPR and Section 165(3) TKG 2021. You may change or withdraw your consent at any time with effect for the future through “Cookie settings” in the footer. The overview there contains the specific technologies, providers, purposes and storage periods used in each case.

10. Google Tag Manager and Google Ads

After you consent, we use Google Tag Manager and Google Ads, provided by Google Ireland Limited, Gordon House, Barrow Street, Dublin 4, Ireland. Tag Manager is used to manage website tags. Google Ads measures the effectiveness of our advertising and, where selected, creates audiences for personalized advertising or remarketing. Information sent to Google may include your IP address, device and browser information, pages visited, referrer, timestamps, interactions and cookie or other online identifiers.

The legal bases are your consent under Article 6(1)(a) GDPR and Section 165(3) TKG 2021. These marketing services are not activated before you consent. Processing by Google LLC in the United States cannot be ruled out. Google may rely on applicable adequacy decisions, in particular the EU–US Data Privacy Framework, or standard contractual clauses.

More information: Google Privacy Policy and Data use in embedded Google services.

11. Google Analytics 4

After you consent, we use Google Analytics 4, a web analytics service provided by Google Ireland Limited, Gordon House, Barrow Street, Dublin 4, Ireland. Google Analytics evaluates how our website is used, including pages visited, time spent, approximate region, device and browser used, and interactions, helping us improve our services. Cookies may be set, in particular “_ga” and “_ga_*”, with storage periods of up to two years; the current details in Cookie settings apply. According to Google, Google Analytics 4 does not log or store IP addresses. We do not use it to identify individual visitors.

The legal bases are your consent under Article 6(1)(a) GDPR and Section 165(3) TKG 2021. Google Analytics is not activated without your consent. Processing by Google LLC in the United States cannot be ruled out. Google may rely on applicable adequacy decisions, in particular the EU–US Data Privacy Framework, or standard contractual clauses. You can withdraw your consent at any time through Cookie settings.

More information: Google Privacy Policy and Data use in embedded Google services.

12. Meta Pixel

After you consent, we use the Meta Pixel, a service provided by Meta Platforms Ireland Limited, Merrion Road, Dublin 4, D04 X2K5, Ireland (“Meta”). The Meta Pixel measures whether visitors reach our website through our Facebook or Instagram ads and which actions they take here (conversion measurement). Where enabled, it may also be used to create advertising audiences (Custom Audiences, remarketing). Cookies may be set, in particular “_fbp” for approximately 90 days, and information such as your IP address, device and browser information, pages visited and timestamps may be sent to Meta. The current details in Cookie settings apply.

We and Meta are joint controllers under Article 26 GDPR for collecting and transmitting this data; Meta is responsible for its subsequent processing. The legal bases are your consent under Article 6(1)(a) GDPR and Section 165(3) TKG 2021. The Meta Pixel is not activated without your consent. Processing by Meta Platforms, Inc. in the United States cannot be ruled out; Meta Platforms, Inc. is certified under the EU–US Data Privacy Framework. You can withdraw your consent at any time through Cookie settings.

More information: Meta Privacy Policy.

13. Leadinfo

After you consent, we use the lead generation service of Leadinfo B.V., Rivium Quadrant 141, 2909 LC Capelle aan den IJssel, the Netherlands. Leadinfo compares a website visitor’s IP address with company data from publicly available sources to associate visits with companies, and provides us with company information and details about pages visited. Leadinfo also processes domains entered in forms to improve the matching of IP addresses to companies and the service.

When the analytics function is enabled, two first-party cookies may be used: “_li_id.*” distinguishes new and returning visits for up to two years, and “_li_ses.*” groups pages visited during a session for the duration of that session. The current details in Cookie settings apply.

The legal bases are your consent under Article 6(1)(a) GDPR and Section 165(3) TKG 2021. Leadinfo is not activated on our website without your consent. You can withdraw consent through Cookie settings and can also use Leadinfo’s opt-out option.

More information: Privacy at Leadinfo; Leadinfo opt-out.

14. Google Maps

We may embed Google Maps, provided by Google Ireland Limited, to show our service area. The interactive map loads only after you consent to the “External media” category or activate the map using the provided two-click solution. Only then is information such as your IP address, device and browser information, and the page visited sent to Google. The legal bases are Article 6(1)(a) GDPR and Section 165(3) TKG 2021. Processing by Google LLC in the United States cannot be ruled out. Without consent, only a local placeholder or a simple link to Google Maps is shown.

15. Social media links

Our website may contain simple links to Instagram, Facebook and LinkedIn. Until you click one of these links, the link itself does not transmit data to the relevant provider. After clicking, you leave our website; the provider’s privacy information applies to subsequent processing.

16. Recipients and transfers to third countries

Where necessary for the relevant purpose, recipients of personal data may include hosting and IT service providers, communications providers, assigned employees and subcontractors, tax advisors, public authorities and the providers named in this notice. Data is transferred only to the extent necessary. For transfers to countries outside the European Economic Area, we use safeguards provided for under the GDPR, in particular adequacy decisions or standard contractual clauses, unless a statutory exception applies.

17. Your rights

Subject to the statutory requirements, you have the right to access, rectification, erasure, restriction of processing and data portability. You may object to processing based on Article 6(1)(f) GDPR for reasons arising from your particular situation. You may withdraw consent you have given at any time with effect for the future. To exercise your rights, a message to office@putzelf.com is sufficient.

You also have the right to lodge a complaint with the Austrian Data Protection Authority, Barichgasse 40-42, 1030 Vienna, telephone +43 1 52 152-0, email dsb@dsb.gv.at.

18. Data security

We take appropriate technical and organizational measures to protect personal data against loss, unauthorized access, alteration and disclosure. The website is transmitted using TLS/SSL encryption.

19. Updates

We update this privacy notice when the services used, processing procedures or the legal situation change. As of: September 10, 2026.
